issues.description: The solution's set_pixel implementation swaps EAX and EBX (xchg eax, ebx) and computes the address using the swapped registers, effectively treating the incoming x and y arguments in reversed order. This contradicts the problem statement (which specifies x in EAX and y in EBX) and the main routine's address calculation (which uses EAX as x and EBX as y). As a result, calling set_pixel will write the pixel at a transposed location (x and y exchanged), causing incorrect behavior and confusing students who follow the specified calling convention.
issues.suggestedFix: Modify the solution's set_pixel so it uses EAX as x and EBX as y (no xchg). Compute byte offset = display_start + (y * 1920 * 4) + (x * 4) (i.e. y*7680 + x*4), then store ecx at that address. Preserve all registers except EAX per the specification (save/restore any temporaries with push/pop).
